section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1969
title: ## ALL INDIA SURVEY During 1969, 1,30,755 deaths were reported in India, which had resulted from accidents of various types. The causes of accidents have been classified into two broad categories viz., (i) Accidents due to acts of nature such as snake bites/animal killing, floods, land-slides etc. and (ii) Accidents due to other causes such as mishappenings in factories, air-crashes, railway accidents etc. The detailed break-up of such accidental deaths in the country due to various causes is furnished in Table I. This Table shows that deaths due to acts of nature account for 29.0% deaths and those due to other causes constitute the remaining 71.0% of the total accidental deaths in the country. Drowning accounted for the highest number of cases (27,079) constituting 20.7% of the total. Animal bite/killing caused deaths in 4,965 cases, while road, railway and fire accidents accounted for 5.4%, 6.0% and 6.9% respectively of total accidental deaths in the country. The pattern of percentage distribution of accidental deaths due to various causes has been more or less the same as during 1966, 1967 and 1968 except for drowning and road accidents. The percentage of deaths on the road has been 5.4 during 1969 as against 4.8 during 1968. The percentage of deaths due to drowning has decreased from 23.1 in 1968 to 20.7 in 1969. TABLE I
